gloss: keep, guard, watch; observe; a charge, a watch
summary: The verb is to keep a thing by watching over it: a garden, a flock, a city, a prisoner, goods left in trust. From that one act come its three great uses. Yahweh keeps his people, “the keeper of Israel” who neither slumbers nor sleeps, and keeps covenant and faithfulness to those who love him. Man keeps Yahweh's commandments, statutes, sabbaths and covenant, which is to hold them carefully and do them (“keep and do”). And a man keeps himself: הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ, “take heed to yourself”. The nouns are the keeping itself: מִשְׁמֶרֶת a charge or duty, a watch, a thing kept; מִשְׁמָר custody and a guard; אַשְׁמוּרָה a watch of the night; שִׁמֻּרִים the night of watching when Israel left Egypt. שְׁמָרִים “lees” and שָׁמִיר “thorn; adamant” are filed under the same letters, the first probably as what is kept in the jar, the second with no tie yet shown.

words.gloss: keep, guard, watch over; observe; take heed
words.summary: About 470 times, nearly all in the qal, and commonest in Deuteronomy, the Psalms and Proverbs. Its core is watching over a thing so that it stays as it should: nothing is lost, nothing gets in or out, nothing is left undone. Whether that is guarding, preserving, confining, storing, observing or obeying depends on what is kept. The participle שֹׁמֵר is the ordinary word for a keeper or watchman.

stems.gloss: keep, have charge of; guard, stand watch; keep safe; keep under guard; watch, mark; store, retain; observe (a commandment, a covenant, a day); guard (one's mouth, way, soul)

senses.definition: To have a thing in one's care and answer for it: a garden, a flock, baggage, goods or animals left in trust, a house, a threshold, the king's person.

evidence.note: Yahweh God put the man in the garden of Eden לְעָבְדָהּ וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ, “to work it and to keep it”: the first use of the verb, the care of what is entrusted.
Cain: הֲשֹׁמֵר אָחִי אָנֹכִי, “am I my brother's keeper?”: a keeper is one who knows where his charge is and answers for him.
“When a man gives his neighbour silver or goods לִשְׁמֹר, and it is stolen from the man's house”: keeping is holding another's goods safe; so of an ass, ox or sheep in Exo 22:9.
Jacob to Laban: “I will again feed your flock, אֶשְׁמֹר.”
“Israel served for a wife, and for a wife שָׁמָר”: he kept sheep.
David left the flock עַל־שֹׁמֵר, with a keeper; in 17:22 his baggage with שׁוֹמֵר הַכֵּלִים, the keeper of the baggage.
The ox that gores, whose owner was warned וְלֹא יִשְׁמְרֶנּוּ, “and did not keep it in”.
The ten concubines David had left לִשְׁמֹר הַבַּיִת, to keep the house.
David to Abner: “why have you not kept watch over (שָׁמַרְתָּ אֶל) your lord the king?”
The priests שֹׁמְרֵי הַסַּף, keepers of the threshold.
Shallum, שֹׁמֵר הַבְּגָדִים, keeper of the garments.
Hegai, the king's eunuch, שֹׁמֵר הַנָּשִׁים, keeper of the women.
Shemaiah, שֹׁמֵר of the east gate.

senses.definition: To stand guard over a place, awake while others sleep: the watchmen of a city, a camp, a wall, and the cherubim at the east of Eden.

evidence.note: “Unless Yahweh יִשְׁמָר־עִיר, in vain the שׁוֹמֵר stays awake (שָׁקַד)”: the keeper of a city is the one who does not sleep.
The cherubim and the flame of the turning sword are set east of the garden לִשְׁמֹר אֶת־דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים, “to keep the way of the tree of life”: to guard it against entry.
“שֹׁמֵר, what of the night? … The שֹׁמֵר said, Morning comes, and also night.”
“My soul is for the Lord more than שֹׁמְרִים for the morning”: watchmen wait out the night.
“On your walls, Jerusalem, I have set שֹׁמְרִים; all the day and all the night they shall never be silent.”
“הַשֹּׁמְרִים who go about the city found me”: the watchmen.
Gideon came at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just set הַשֹּׁמְרִים, the guards.
“Make the watch strong, set up שֹׁמְרִים.”
The guard of the king's house and of the house of Yahweh, by thirds.
Gatekeepers, שֹׁמְרִים, a guard at the storehouses of the gates.

senses.definition: To keep a person from harm, chiefly of Yahweh keeping his people: on a journey, from evil, from the wicked, in going out and coming in.

evidence.note: “He who keeps you will not slumber … שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל neither slumbers nor sleeps. Yahweh is your keeper … Yahweh will keep you from all evil, he will keep your soul; Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in”: the verb six times.
To Jacob: “I am with you, וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ wherever you go, and will bring you back to this ground”; Jacob's vow answers in 28:20.
The priests' blessing: יְבָרֶכְךָ יַהְוֶה וְיִשְׁמְרֶךָ, “Yahweh bless you and keep you.”
“I send an angel before you לִשְׁמָרְךָ בַּדָּרֶךְ”, to keep you in the way.
“He will give his angels charge over you, לִשְׁמָרְךָ in all your ways”; quoted in Luk 4:10.
Psa 91:11 quoted: “to guard you” (τοῦ διαφυλάξαι σε).
Yahweh “kept us in all the way in which we went”.
“The feet of his faithful ones he will keep.”
“He keeps all his bones; not one of them is broken.”
“Yahweh keeps all who love him, and all the wicked he will destroy.”
“Yahweh keeps the sojourners.”
“Keep me, God, for I take refuge in you.”
“You, Yahweh, will keep them; you will guard him from this generation for ever.”
Of discretion: “it will keep watch over you (תִּשְׁמֹר עָלֶיךָ), understanding will guard you”.

senses.gloss: keep under guard, watch (a prisoner, a house)
senses.definition: To guard someone so that he does not get away, or watch a place to take him.

evidence.note: “Roll great stones to the mouth of the cave and set men over it לְשָׁמְרָם”, to guard the five kings.
“שְׁמֹר this man; if he is missing, your life shall be for his life.”
Saul sent messengers to David's house לְשָׁמְרוֹ, to watch it, and to kill him in the morning.
“If I sinned, וּשְׁמַרְתָּנִי, and you would not clear me of my iniquity.”

senses.definition: To keep the eyes on a thing: to watch a person's mouth or steps, mark a man or his sins, lie in wait for his fall, look at the wind, know the time of a thing.

evidence.note: As Hannah prayed long, “Eli שֹׁמֵר אֶת־פִּיהָ”, was watching her mouth.
“If you, Yah, should mark iniquities (עֲוֺנוֹת תִּשְׁמָר), Lord, who shall stand?”
“You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths”; so Job 33:11.
“They watch my heels, as they have waited for my soul.”
“Those who watch for my soul (שֹׁמְרֵי נַפְשִׁי) take counsel together.”
“Every man of my peace, watching for my stumbling (שֹׁמְרֵי צַלְעִי).”
“Mark the blameless (שְׁמָר־תָּם) and see the upright.”
“He who watches the wind (שֹׁמֵר רוּחַ) will not sow.”
“Do you watch the calving of the hinds?”
The turtledove, swift and crane “keep the time of their coming”.
“When Joab was watching the city (בִּשְׁמוֹר … אֶל־הָעִיר)”: besieging it.
“One high above the high is watching.”

senses.definition: To keep a thing and not let it go: food laid up, a saying kept in mind, knowledge on the lips, anger kept for ever; set against throwing away.

evidence.note: “Let them gather all the food of these good years … and heap up grain, food in the cities, וְשָׁמָרוּ”: and keep it.
“A time לִשְׁמוֹר and a time to cast away (לְהַשְׁלִיךְ).”
“His brothers envied him, but his father שָׁמַר אֶת־הַדָּבָר”: kept the saying in mind.
“Keep them in the midst of your heart.”
“The lips of a priest should keep knowledge.”
Edom: “his fury, he kept it (שְׁמָרָה) for ever”.
“Will he keep (anger) for ever?”, beside נָטַר.

senses.gloss: keep, observe (a commandment, a covenant, a day)
senses.definition: To keep what Yahweh has commanded: to hold it carefully and do it. Its objects are his commandments, statutes, judgments, testimonies, way, word, covenant, sabbaths and feasts. It is joined again and again to “do” (שָׁמַר לַעֲשׂוֹת, “keep and do”), so the keeping is not the doing itself but the care that leads to it.

evidence.note: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם וַעֲשִׂיתֶם, “keep and do, for that is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples”.
“Every word that I command you, אֹתוֹ תִשְׁמְרוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת; you shall not add to it nor take from it”: keeping is doing it whole, as given (so Deu 4:2).
“You shall keep my statutes and my judgments, which a man shall do and live by them.”
Abraham will command his sons and his house after him, וְשָׁמְרוּ דֶּרֶךְ יַהְוֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט: “they shall keep the way of Yahweh, to do righteousness and judgment”.
“You shall keep my covenant, you and your seed after you.”
“Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes and my laws.”
“You shall keep the unleavened bread … you shall keep this day throughout your generations.”
“Surely my sabbaths you shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you”; so 31:16.
“שָׁמוֹר the sabbath day to sanctify it”, where Exo 20:8 has זָכוֹר, “remember”.
Faithfulness to thousands, “to those who love me and keep my commandments”.
“Hear, Israel, וְשָׁמַרְתָּ לַעֲשׂוֹת.”
The king reads the law all his days “to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them”.
He gave them the lands of the nations “so that they might keep his statutes and guard his laws”.
“By what shall a young man make his path clean? By keeping it according to your word.”
“Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law contend with them.”
“Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of man.”
“Keep judgment and do righteousness … who keeps the sabbath from profaning it, and keeps his hand from doing any evil.”
“I will put my spirit within you and make you walk in my statutes, and my judgments you shall keep and do.”
Judah “rejected the law of Yahweh and did not keep his statutes”.
“If you would enter into life, keep the commandments” (τήρησον τὰς ἐντολάς): the keeping and living of Lev 18:5.
“Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it” (φυλάσσοντες): hear and keep, as Deu 6:3.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to keep his covenant and his faithfulness to those who love him, and to keep what he has sworn or spoken. Of men: to keep faith, an oath, a king's command.

evidence.note: “The faithful God, שֹׁמֵר הַבְּרִית וְהַחֶסֶד to those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations”: he keeps, and they keep.
“Because you hear these judgments and keep and do them, Yahweh your God will keep for you the covenant and the faithfulness which he swore to your fathers.”
Solomon: “keeping the covenant and the faithfulness to your servants who walk before you with all their heart”.
“The righteous nation that keeps faith (שֹׁמֵר אֱמֻנִים).”
“Keep faithfulness and judgment, and wait for your God continually.”
“Keep the king's command, because of the oath of God.”

senses.definition: To keep watch over oneself: the mouth and tongue, the way, the soul (life). He who guards his mouth keeps his life.

evidence.note: “He who guards (נֹצֵר) his mouth keeps (שֹׁמֵר) his soul; he who opens wide his lips, ruin is his.”
“He who keeps his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles.”
“I will keep my ways from sinning with my tongue; I will keep a muzzle on my mouth.”
“He who keeps a commandment keeps his soul; he who despises his ways shall die.”
“He who guards his way keeps his soul.”
“He who keeps his soul will be far from” thorns and snares.
“Take heed to yourself and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget.”
“From her who lies in your bosom keep the doors of your mouth.”

senses.definition: To hold to worthless things, idols, as others keep Yahweh's word.

evidence.note: “I hate those who keep worthless vanities (הַשֹּׁמְרִים הַבְלֵי־שָׁוא), but I trust in Yahweh.”

stems.gloss: take heed, be on one's guard; keep oneself from; be kept

senses.definition: To keep watch over oneself. Most often the command הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ, “take heed to yourself”, followed by פֶּן “lest” or אַל “do not” and the thing to be avoided; with מִן, to be on guard against someone or something.

evidence.note: רַק הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ וּשְׁמֹר נַפְשְׁךָ מְאֹד פֶּן־תִּשְׁכַּח: the niphal and the qal side by side, “take heed to yourself and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget”.
“Take heed to yourself lest you forget Yahweh your God, so as not to keep his commandments.”
Abraham: “Take heed to yourself lest you take my son back there.”
God to Laban in a dream: “Take heed to yourself lest you speak with Jacob from good to bad.”
Pharaoh to Moses: “Take heed to yourself; see my face no more.”
“Take heed to yourselves, going up into the mountain or touching its edge.”
Of the angel sent before Israel: הִשָּׁמֶר מִפָּנָיו, “be on your guard before him and hear his voice”.
“Take heed to yourself lest you make a covenant with the inhabitant of the land.”
וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם מְאֹד לְנַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם, “take great heed to your souls, for you saw no form”; so Jos 23:11.
“Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see.”
Jonathan to David: “take heed to yourself in the morning, and stay in a secret place”.
“Take heed of passing this place” … “and he was on his guard there, not once nor twice”.
To Ahaz: הִשָּׁמֵר וְהַשְׁקֵט, “take heed and be quiet; do not fear”.
“Take heed for your souls, and carry no burden on the sabbath day.”
“Take heed to your spirit, and do not deal treacherously.”
“Take heed to yourselves lest (προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε) your hearts be weighed down”: the Greek of הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם פֶּן.

senses.definition: To keep away from a thing.

evidence.note: The holy bread may be given “if the young men have kept themselves (נִשְׁמְרוּ) only from women”.
Of Manoah's wife: “from all that I said to the woman let her keep herself”; 13:4 names wine, strong drink and anything unclean.
In the camp, “keep yourself from every evil thing”.

senses.definition: The passive of the qal's “keep safe”.

evidence.note: “By a prophet Yahweh brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet he was kept (נִשְׁמָר)”, answering Jacob's keeping of sheep in 12:13.
“He does not forsake his faithful ones; they are kept (נִשְׁמָרוּ) for ever, but the seed of the wicked is cut off.”

senses.definition: Once, a participle, of those who hold to idols; Psa 31:7 says the same with the qal.

evidence.note: מְשַׁמְּרִים הַבְלֵי־שָׁוְא חַסְדָּם יַעֲזֹבוּ: “those who keep worthless vanities forsake their own faithfulness”; keeping set against forsaking.

senses.definition: To guard oneself against one's own iniquity.

evidence.note: “I was blameless toward him, וָאֶשְׁתַּמְּרָה מֵעֲוֺנִי”: and I kept myself from my iniquity. The same line in Psa 18:24.

senses.definition: Of statutes: to be kept by a people.

evidence.note: “The statutes of Omri are kept (וְיִשְׁתַּמֵּר), and all the work of the house of Ahab, and you walk in their counsels”: the statutes of the king who built Samaria, kept in place of Yahweh's.

evidence.locator: Gen.2.15 and Gen.3.24, לשמר → φυλάσσειν; Lev.18.5 → φυλάξεσθε; Num.6.24 → φυλάξαι; Deu.7.9 → φυλάσσων; Psa.121.4 → φυλάσσων; φυλάσσω renders שָׁמַר ×274

evidence.note: “Those who hear the word of God and keep it.”
Stephen: “you who received the law … and did not keep it.”
The young man, of the commandments: “all these I have kept from my youth.”
Shepherds “keeping watches of the night (φυλάσσοντες φυλακὰς τῆς νυκτός) over their flock”: the verb with its noun, as שָׁמַר מִשְׁמֶרֶת, and of a flock as Gen 30:31.
“I kept them in your name … I guarded (ἐφύλαξα) them, and none of them is lost.”
“The Lord is faithful, who will establish you and keep you from the evil”: as Psa 121:7.
“To him who is able to keep you from stumbling.”
“He who hates his soul in this world will keep it to life eternal”: keeping one's soul, as Pro 19:16.
“Keep yourselves from idols.”
“Guard the deposit”: a thing given in trust to keep, as Exo 22:6.

evidence.locator: Psa.91.11, לִשְׁמָרְךָ → διαφυλάξαι; διαφυλάσσω renders שָׁמַר ×13

evidence.note: Psa 91:11 quoted, its only use in the New Testament.

evidence.locator: Pro.19.16 and Pro.13.3, שֹׁמֵר → τηρεῖ; Ecc.11.4 → τηρῶν; Sng.3.3 → τηροῦντες; Dan.9.4 → τηρῶν; with διατηρέω at Gen.17.9, Gen.17.10 → διατηρήσεις; τηρέω renders שָׁמַר ×9, διατηρέω ×6

evidence.note: “If you would enter into life, keep the commandments.”
“If you love me, keep my commandments”: love and keeping together, as Deu 7:9.
“This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments.”
“Holy Father, keep them in your name”; 17:15, “keep them from the evil”.
The saints, “those keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus”; so Rev 12:17.

evidence.locator: Gen.24.6, Exo.34.12, Deu.4.9, Deu.6.12, Deu.12.13, הִשָּׁמֶר → πρόσεχε; προσέχω renders שָׁמַר ×16, the niphal

evidence.note: “Take heed to yourselves lest …”
“Take heed to yourselves.”
To the elders of Ephesus: “take heed to yourselves and to all the flock … to shepherd the ecclesia of God”.
“Beware of (προσέχετε ἀπό) the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees”: as the niphal with מִן.

parallels.note: “Guard, keep”: the commonest parallel, in every sense of the verb.

evidence.note: Of Levi: “they kept (שָׁמְרוּ) your word and guard (יִנְצֹרוּ) your covenant.”

parallels.note: “Do”: to keep is to do, and the two stand together throughout the law.

evidence.note: “Happy are those who keep judgment, he who does righteousness at every time.”

parallels.note: “Hear”: hearing comes first and keeping follows it.

evidence.note: שְׁמֹר וְשָׁמַעְתָּ, “keep and hear all these words”.

parallels.note: “Remember”: the sabbath command has “remember” in Exodus and “keep” in Deuteronomy.

evidence.note: “To those who keep his covenant and remember his precepts to do them.”

parallels.note: “Keep (anger)”: the verb that answers שָׁמַר in Aramaic, here in Hebrew beside it.

evidence.note: “Will he keep (יִנְטֹר) for ever, will he hold (יִשְׁמֹר) to the end?”

opposites.note: “Forsake, leave”: the regular opposite, of the law, of instruction, of Yahweh's charge.

evidence.note: “He who keeps instruction is a path to life, but he who forsakes reproof leads astray.”
“We keep the charge of Yahweh our God, but you have forsaken him.”
Of wisdom: “do not forsake her and she will keep you.”

opposites.note: “Forget”: what is not kept is forgotten.
“Destroy”, set against Yahweh's keeping in a play on the sound: שׁוֹמֵר … יַשְׁמִיד.
“Profane”: the sabbath is kept or profaned.

phrases.gloss: keep to do, be careful to do
keeper of the covenant and the faithfulness (of Yahweh)
keepers of the threshold (priests at the door of the house)
one who keeps his soul (his life)

words.gloss: charge, duty; watch, post; a thing kept
words.summary: The noun of the verb in all its chief senses, and most often its own object: שָׁמַר מִשְׁמֶרֶת, “keep the keeping”. In Numbers it is the Levites' charge of the tabernacle and its vessels; elsewhere what Yahweh requires to be kept, a watchman's post, and a thing laid up to be kept.

senses.definition: What a man or a house is given to keep and answers for: the Levites' and priests' charge of the tabernacle, its vessels, the holy place and the altar; and so a turn or post of service.

evidence.note: The Levites “shall keep his charge (מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ) and the charge of all the congregation before the tent of meeting, to do the service of the tabernacle”.
“The charge of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting: the tabernacle and the tent, its covering and the screen”: the charge is named as a list of things.
The Levites camp around the tabernacle and keep its charge, so that there is no wrath on the congregation.
“You shall keep the charge of the holy place and the charge of the altar.”
Moses, Aaron and his sons on the east, “keeping the charge of the sanctuary for the charge of the sons of Israel; and the stranger who comes near shall be put to death”.
Aaron and his sons stay at the door of the tent seven days and “keep the charge of Yahweh”, that they do not die.
The sons of Zadok “kept the charge of my sanctuary when the sons of Israel went astray from me”.
Abijah: the daily offerings, incense, bread and lamps, “for we keep the charge of Yahweh our God”.
“They kept the charge of their God and the charge of the purification.”
“I set up מִשְׁמָרוֹת for the priests and for the Levites, each in his work”: posts of duty.
“The priests stood at their posts (מִשְׁמְרוֹתָם).”
The singers cast lots for their duty, small and great alike.
Benjamin had till then been “keeping the charge of the house of Saul”: allegiance.

senses.gloss: charge (what Yahweh requires to be kept)
senses.definition: What Yahweh has given to be kept, set beside his commandments, statutes and laws.

evidence.note: “Abraham obeyed my voice and kept מִשְׁמַרְתִּי, my commandments, my statutes and my laws.”
“You shall keep my charge, so as not to do any of the abominable statutes that were done before you.”
“You shall love Yahweh your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his judgments and his commandments, all the days.”
When the cloud stayed many days on the tabernacle, “the sons of Israel kept the charge of Yahweh and did not set out”.
To Joshua the high priest: “if you walk in my ways and if you keep my charge”.
“It is vain to serve God; what profit is it that we have kept his charge?”

senses.definition: A thing set by to be kept, for a time or for the generations to come.

evidence.note: The Pesach lamb, taken on the tenth day, “shall be to you לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת until the fourteenth day of this month”.
An omer of manna laid up before Yahweh “לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת for your generations, that they may see the bread”.
What is left over of the manna on the sixth day is laid up “to be kept until the morning”.
Aaron's rod put back before the testimony “to be kept as a sign”.
The ashes of the heifer laid up outside the camp, kept for the water of impurity.
“I have given you the keeping of my heave offerings.”

senses.definition: The watch a guard keeps, and the place where he stands.

evidence.note: “On the watchtower, Lord, I stand continually by day, and on מִשְׁמַרְתִּי I am stationed all the nights.”
“On מִשְׁמַרְתִּי I will stand, and station myself on the rampart, and look out to see what he will speak with me.”
“Set watches (מִשְׁמְרוֹת) of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each in his watch and each before his house.”
The watch of the king's house and of the house of Yahweh.
The gatekeepers lodged around the house of God, “for the watch was on them”.

senses.definition: The state of being kept: safe keeping with a protector, or confinement.

evidence.note: David to Abiathar: “Stay with me, do not fear … for you are מִשְׁמֶרֶת with me”: in safe keeping.
David put the ten concubines in בֵּית־מִשְׁמֶרֶת, a house of keeping, “shut up to the day of their death”.

evidence.locator: Num.3.7, מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ and מִשְׁמֶרֶת → φυλακάς; φυλακή renders מִשְׁמֶרֶת ×45

evidence.note: “Keeping watches (φυλάσσοντες φυλακάς) of the night over their flock.”

words.summary: The masculine noun, twenty-two times: in the law, the place where a man is held; in Nehemiah and Chronicles, a guard and a division of those on duty.

senses.definition: Being held under guard, and the place of it: where Joseph's fellow prisoners and his brothers were kept, and where a man was held until Yahweh's judgment on him was made known.

evidence.note: Pharaoh put his two officers “בְּמִשְׁמַר, in the house of the chief of the guard, in the prison, the place where Joseph was bound”.
Joseph “gathered them into מִשְׁמָר three days”; 42:19, “your house of custody”.
The blasphemer: “they put him בַּמִּשְׁמָר, for it to be declared to them at the mouth of Yahweh”; so the sabbath-breaker in Num 15:34.

senses.definition: A body of men set to guard, or the guard they keep.

evidence.note: “We prayed to our God and set a מִשְׁמָר against them day and night.”
“Let each man and his servant lodge within Jerusalem, and they shall be to us a guard by night and labour by day.”
“The men of the guard who followed me.”
“Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set a guard over me?”
“Make the guard strong, set up watchmen.”
To Gog: “you shall be to them לְמִשְׁמָר.”

senses.definition: A turn of duty of the Levites and gatekeepers, watch answering to watch; and in the plural the observances of the house of God.

evidence.note: The heads of the Levites and their brothers opposite them to praise and give thanks, מִשְׁמָר לְעֻמַּת מִשְׁמָר, “watch against watch”.
The gatekeepers on the west, “watch against watch”.
“Do not wipe out my faithful deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for its observances (וּבְמִשְׁמָרָיו).”

senses.definition: Whatever is kept under guard, once.

evidence.note: מִכָּל־מִשְׁמָר נְצֹר לִבֶּךָ: “above all that is guarded, guard your heart, for out of it are the goings out of life.”

evidence.locator: Gen.40.3, בְּמִשְׁמַר → ἐν φυλακῇ; φυλακή renders מִשְׁמָר ×11

evidence.note: Herod put Peter “in prison (εἰς φυλακήν), delivering him to four quaternions of soldiers to guard (φυλάσσειν) him”: custody and its guard, as Gen 40:3.

words.summary: Seven times, also spelled אַשְׁמֹרֶת: a division of the night, as long as one guard stands before the next relieves him. Judges 7:19 names “the middle watch”, which makes three; Exodus 14:24 and 1 Samuel 11:11 name the last, “the watch of the morning”. The New Testament counts four (Mat 14:25).

senses.definition: One of the parts into which the night is divided by the changing of the guard; in the plural, the wakeful hours of the night.

evidence.note: Gideon came to the edge of the camp “at the beginning of the middle watch (הָאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַתִּיכוֹנָה); they had only just set the guards (הַשֹּׁמְרִים)”: the watch is the guards' turn, and there is a first, a middle and a last.
“In the watch of the morning (בְּאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַבֹּקֶר) Yahweh looked down on the camp of Egypt.”
Saul came into the camp “in the watch of the morning” and struck Ammon until the heat of the day.
“A thousand years in your eyes are as yesterday when it passes, וְאַשְׁמוּרָה בַלָּיְלָה, and a watch in the night”: a few hours, gone unnoticed by the sleeper.
“Rise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches.”
“When I remember you on my bed, in the watches I meditate on you.”
“My eyes are awake before the watches, to meditate on your word.”
“In the fourth watch of the night (τετάρτῃ φυλακῇ τῆς νυκτός) Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.”
“If he comes in the second watch, or in the third, and finds them so, blessed are those servants.”

evidence.locator: Jdg.7.19, הָאַשְׁמֹרֶת → τῆς φυλακῆς; 1Sa.11.11 → φυλακῇ; Psa.90.4, אַשְׁמוּרָה → φυλακή

evidence.note: “If the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have watched.”

words.summary: Five times, only in the plural (the singular would be שֶׁמֶר): the sediment that settles in wine left standing. Its tie to “keep” is not certain. The likeliest is “what is kept”: wine left on its lees is wine kept long in the jar, not poured off, which is how Jer 48:11 and Isa 25:6 use the word; Arabic ثُمَالَة, “what remains in the bottom of a vessel”, from a verb “remain; leave, reserve”, has a like sense but shows ṯ and l where Hebrew has שׁ and ר, so it is recorded only as possible. No cognate certainly shares its meaning; it rests on its kinship with the verb’s “keep, store” and with מִשְׁמֶרֶת “a thing kept”.

senses.definition: The sediment at the bottom of a wine jar. Wine left undisturbed on its lees keeps its taste and smell; wine “of lees”, strained, is old and good; the dregs themselves are the last and worst of the cup.

evidence.note: “Moab has been at ease from his youth, settled on his lees (שֹׁקֵט אֶל־שְׁמָרָיו), and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel … so his taste remains in him and his scent is not changed”: the lees are what wine sits on when it is not poured off.
Yahweh's feast for all peoples on this mountain: מִשְׁתֵּה שְׁמָרִים … שְׁמָרִים מְזֻקָּקִים, “a feast of lees … lees refined”: wine kept on its lees and then strained.
“The men who thicken on their lees, who say in their heart, Yahweh will not do good, nor will he do evil”: settled and undisturbed, as Moab.
The cup in Yahweh's hand: “surely its dregs (שְׁמָרֶיהָ) all the wicked of the earth shall drain and drink”: what is left at the bottom.

evidence.locator: Isa.25.6, שְׁמָרִים → οἶνον (πίονται οἶνον): the Greek gives “wine” for the lees here and has no one word for them elsewhere

evidence.note: “No one having drunk old wine wishes for new, for he says, The old is better”: wine that has been kept, as the wine of Isa 25:6.

words.gloss: thorn, briar; adamant (a very hard stone)
words.summary: Eleven times as a common noun, in two senses that scripture never joins: a thorn bush (eight times, all in Isaiah, and always with שַׁיִת) and a stone harder than flint (three times). How either goes back to the root is not understood. Nothing in scripture ties them to “keep”, and the cognates point elsewhere: the stone is Aramaic שָׁמִירָא and may be a trade name for emery that passed between languages; the thorn has only a possible link in Arabic سَمُر, a thorny acacia. So the thorn has nothing for it and the root’s other cognates, the stone’s Aramaic among them, count against it (balance −4). The same spelling is also a place (Jos 15:48; Jdg 10:1–2) and a Levite (1Ch 24:24), which the count of uses includes.

senses.definition: The thorny growth that takes over a vineyard or a land left untilled, and is fuel for fire. Always beside שַׁיִת (שָׁמִיר וָשַׁיִת, “briar and thorn”), except Isa 32:13, where it is beside קוֹץ.

evidence.note: The vineyard laid waste: “it shall not be pruned nor hoed, וְעָלָה שָׁמִיר וָשָׁיִת”: what comes up where a vineyard is not tended.
Where there were a thousand vines, “it shall be for briar and thorn”; men go there with bow and arrows, and no one comes to the hoed hills “for fear of briar and thorn”.
“Wickedness burns as fire; it eats briar and thorn.”
The light of Israel shall burn and eat “his thorn and his briar in one day”: of Assyria's host.
“Who will give me briar and thorn? In battle I would march against it; I would burn it together.”
“On the ground of my people thorn and briar shall come up.”

senses.gloss: adamant, a stone harder than flint
senses.definition: A stone of the greatest hardness, used as the point of an engraving tool, and a figure for a forehead or heart that will not yield.

evidence.note: כְּשָׁמִיר חָזָק מִצֹּר נָתַתִּי מִצְחֶךָ: “as שָׁמִיר, harder than flint, I have made your forehead.”
“The sin of Judah is written with a pen of iron, with a point of שָׁמִיר (בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר), engraved on the tablet of their heart”: it cuts what iron cuts.
“They made their heart שָׁמִיר, so as not to hear the law.”

words.summary: Once, as a noun (Psa 141:3). The other tokens counted under this spelling are the verb: the imperative שָׁמְרָה “keep!” (Psa 25:20; 86:2) and the perfect “she has kept” (Psa 119:167; Job 10:12; 24:15).

senses.definition: A guard posted over something, here over the mouth.

evidence.note: שִׁיתָה יַהְוֶה שָׁמְרָה לְפִי נִצְּרָה עַל־דַּל שְׂפָתָי: “Set, Yahweh, a guard for my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips”, with נָצַר in the parallel line.

words.summary: Twice, in one verse, in the plural: the night of the Pesach. Yahweh kept watch that night to bring Israel out, and Israel keeps the night for him in every generation, so the one word is both the watching and the observing.

senses.definition: A keeping awake and a keeping of a night: first Yahweh's, then Israel's.

evidence.note: לֵיל שִׁמֻּרִים הוּא לַיַהְוֶה לְהוֹצִיאָם מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם … שִׁמֻּרִים לְכָל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְדֹרֹתָם: “a night of watching it is for Yahweh, to bring them out of the land of Egypt; this same night is for Yahweh, a watching for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.”
The same chapter's verb: “you shall keep this day throughout your generations.”

words.summary: Once, in the plural with “my eyes”. The form is the passive participle “kept, guarded” used as a noun; “eyelids” (the guards of the eye, or what keeps it shut) fits the verse, in which the psalmist cannot sleep, but one verse fixes little, and “you hold my eyes' watches” (keep my eyes on watch) is possible.

senses.definition: What is held in a sleepless night so that the eyes stay open.

evidence.note: אָחַזְתָּ שְׁמֻרוֹת עֵינָי נִפְעַמְתִּי וְלֹא אֲדַבֵּר: “you have taken hold of the שְׁמֻרוֹת of my eyes; I am troubled and cannot speak”; the verse before is of the night and the spirit fainting.

cognates.note: Punic has the verb in a prayer formula with nṣr, “keep and protect”, the same pair as Hebrew שָׁמַר and נָצַר (Deu 33:9; Pro 13:3); the participle as a title, “watchman of the quarry”, as Hebrew שֹׁמֵר; and names of the type šmrbʿl, “Baal protect”, as Hebrew שְׁמַרְיָהוּ. Phoenician writes one letter for š and ṯ, so it does not show which stands behind the ש.

evidence.locator: p. 470, Š-M-R I (v. qal KEEP, GUARD, PROTECT; RES 19.1, RES 20.1); ŠMR II (n.m. WATCHMAN, GUARD; KAI 62.7); ŠMR III and ŠMRBʿL (names, “DN protect!”)

cognates.note: The Targums' word for the Hebrew niphal הִשָּׁמֶר, in the reflexive stem, written with ס (some copies with שׁ or ט). Aramaic turns the older ṯ into t (as תּוֹר for שׁוֹר), so a sibilant here speaks for š behind the ש of “keep”, unless the Targums simply took the word over from the Hebrew they were rendering. Aramaic's own verb for “keep” is נְטַר, and the Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra and the Peshitta do not use this root.

evidence.locator: O01138, סְמַר II (= h. שָׁמַר), Ithpa. אִסְתַּמַּר, to take heed, beware: Targ. O. Exo 23:21; Targ. Jos 6:18; Targ. Job 36:21

cognates.gloss: he stayed awake, did not sleep; he held talk by night
cognates.note: Waking through the night is what a watchman does (Psa 127:1, “in vain the keeper stays awake”) and what the night watch and the “night of watching” are named for. Arabic s answers Hebrew שׁ where the older sound is š. The Arabic has no sense “guard”, so the link is only possible.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1424, art. سمر, 1 سَمَرَ
evidence.note: “He held a conversation, or discourse, by night: or he waked; continued awake; did not sleep”; سَامِرٌ, p. 1426, persons waking, not sleeping.

cognates.gloss: one who aids and manages the affairs of his people; their stay, refuge, protector
cognates.note: From ثَمَلَ “he remained; he was a support to, aided, fed and managed the affairs of” (orphans, his tribe). The sense is near “keeper”, but the last letter is l where Hebrew has r, so the match is not regular. If it holds, the ש of “keep” would be ṯ, against the š of the Aramaic and of سَمَرَ.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 353, art. ثمل, 1 ثَمَلَ; p. 354, ثِمَالٌ
evidence.note: ثَمَلَهُمْ “he aided them, or succoured them, and undertook, or managed, their affairs”; ثِمَالٌ “their stay, or support … a refuge, or protector”.

cognates.gloss: what remains in the bottom of a vessel or trough; froth
cognates.note: With ثُمْلَة “a little water remaining in the bottom of a vessel”, ثَمْلَة “mud taken from the bottom of a well”, and ثَمَّلَ “he left it, reserved it”. Near in sense to שְׁמָרִים, what is left at the bottom of the wine, but with l for Hebrew r. It shows ṯ.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 354, art. ثمل, ثُمْلَةٌ, ثَمْلَةٌ and ثُمَالَةٌ; 2 ثمّل
evidence.note: “A remainder, or water remaining, or a little water remaining, in the bottom of a watering-trough, or of a skin, or of a vessel of any kind”; ثمّلهُ “he made it to remain; he left it; or reserved it”.

cognates.gloss: a kind of gum-acacia tree, with small leaves and short thorns
cognates.note: A thorny tree of dry country, as שָׁמִיר is the thorn of untilled land. The likeness is of sound and of kind only; Hebrew also has a root סמר “bristle” (מַסְמֵר “nail”, Arabic مِسْمَار) to which the Arabic may belong instead.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1425, art. سمر, سَمُرٌ
evidence.note: “A certain kind of tree … [a species] of the طَلْح, of the kind called عِضَاه, having small leaves, short thorns, and a yellow fruit.”

cognates.note: The Targums use it not only where the Hebrew has שָׁמִיר (Ezk 3:9; Zec 7:12) but for חַלָּמִישׁ “flint” (Psa 114:8; Job 28:9), so it was a word of Aramaic in its own right, for a very hard stone.

evidence.locator: U01479, שָׁמִיר, שָׁמִירָא: 1) flint, Targ. Psa 114:8; Targ. Job 28:9; 2) diamond, Targ. Ezk 3:9; Targ. Zec 7:12

doctrine.statement: Yahweh God put the man in the garden “to work it and to keep it” (Gen 2:15): the first thing kept in scripture is a trust given to man. When the man had not kept the one command, Yahweh God said, “lest he put out his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever” (Gen 3:22), drove him out, and set the cherubim and the flame of the sword “to keep the way of the tree of life” (Gen 3:24); the man was told, “dust you are, and to dust you shall return” (Gen 3:19). From the verses: living for ever was not something the man had in himself. It lay in a tree he had not yet eaten of, and he was shut out from it so that he should die. But the way was kept, not closed: a guarded way is one that still leads there. “To him who overcomes I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God” (Rev 2:7), and those who do his commandments have right to it (Rev 22:14).

Yahweh knew Abraham, that he would command his house after him “and they shall keep the way of Yahweh, to do righteousness and judgment, so that Yahweh may bring on Abraham what he has spoken of him” (Gen 18:19); and the promises were confirmed to Isaac “because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge” (Gen 26:5). The law says, “you shall keep my statutes and my judgments, which a man shall do and live by them” (Lev 18:5), and the keeping is always for doing: “keep and do” (Deu 4:6), nothing added and nothing taken away (Deu 13:1). He keeps covenant and faithfulness “to those who love him and keep his commandments” (Deu 7:9). Israel “received the law and did not keep it” (Act 7:53; Amo 2:4), and Yahweh promised, “I will put my spirit within you and make you walk in my statutes, and my judgments you shall keep and do” (Ezk 36:27). Jesus says the same as Moses: “if you would enter into life, keep the commandments” (Mat 19:17); “if you love me, keep my commandments” (Jhn 14:15); “blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it” (Luk 11:28). The saints are “those keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus” (Rev 14:12). From the verses: to keep is more than to hear or to know. It is to hold a word carefully and do it, out of love for the one who gave it, and life is promised to those who do. “Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of man” (Ecc 12:13).

Yahweh promised Jacob, “I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this ground” (Gen 28:15), and the priests were to put his name on Israel with the words “Yahweh bless you and keep you” (Num 6:24). Psalm 121 calls him “the keeper of Israel” who neither slumbers nor sleeps: “Yahweh will keep you from all evil; he will keep your soul; Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in, from now and for ever” (Psa 121:4, 7–8). He does it by his angels: “I send an angel before you to keep you in the way” (Exo 23:20); “he will give his angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways” (Psa 91:11, quoted in Luk 4:10). “Yahweh keeps all who love him, and all the wicked he will destroy” (Psa 145:20). Jesus, about to leave his disciples, asks this keeping of God: “Holy Father, keep them in your name … while I was with them I kept them in your name … I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil” (Jhn 17:11–12, 15). From the verses: the keeper is the Father, whom the son asks; the son kept those given him while he was with them; and the keeping is not removal from the world or from trouble but preservation through it, “kept by the power of God through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time” (1Pe 1:5).

The night Israel left Egypt was “a night of watching for Yahweh, to bring them out”, and so “a watching for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations” (Exo 12:42): he kept watch to save, and they keep the night for him. The watchman's work is to stay awake until morning: “my soul is for the Lord more than watchmen for the morning” (Psa 130:6); “Watchman, what of the night? … Morning comes, and also night” (Isa 21:11–12); “on my watch I will stand … and look out to see what he will speak” (Hab 2:1). Jesus speaks of his own coming in the same terms: “if he comes in the second watch, or in the third, and finds them so, blessed are those servants” (Luk 12:38); “if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief was coming, he would have watched” (Mat 24:43). From the verses: those who wait for him are set as men on a night watch, who do not know the hour and are to be found awake.

note: Drafted 2026-11-15. Root key שמר, as BDB and the corpus key it; no other entry has it. Sounds behind ש: the evidence does not settle them. For “keep”, Targum Aramaic אִסְתַּמַּר (a sibilant, not t) and Arabic samara “stay awake” point to š; the proposal that the root is ṯmr rests on Aramaic and Syriac תמרא / ܬܡܪܐ “eyelid” (beside Psa 77:5) and Arabic ṯamala, of which only the Arabic could be verified in a dictionary here, and it has l for r. For “lees” the only candidate (Arabic ṯumāla) shows ṯ, also with l for r. So lees may be an older ṯ-root distinct from “keep” (š), or the same root with its sense “what is kept, left”; both are recorded as possible and the split is not asserted. שָׁמִיר “adamant” has its own Aramaic cognate and looks like a travelling word for emery; שָׁמִיר “thorn” has no sure cognate. BDB files lees (v.eg) and שָׁמִיר (v.eh) as separate roots; they are kept here under the one spelling, as the README directs. Leads not followed (no verifiable locator): Syriac ܬܡܪܐ “eyelid” (Payne Smith; SEDRA has only the name Tamar under TMR) and Jewish Aramaic תִּמּוּרְתָּא “eyelid” (not found in the vendored Jastrow); Ugaritic šmr, claimed by Klein, not found in Segert's glossary or Fisher; Akkadian šamāru in Oracc means “rage; praise”, not “guard”, and was left out as not sharing the meaning; Mandaic סמירא “preserved” (Klein); Egyptian jsmr “[a mineral]” (TLA tla31530) and Greek σμύρις “emery” for שָׁמִיר: direction of borrowing unknown, so not entered as loans; Sabaean msmrn (Biella p. 546 area, fragmentary). The Krahmalkov citation was read from the pdftotext layer of the scan (headwords print Š as S there); check the page before sign-off. Token counts: the brief counts by spelling, so v.ef.aa (470) includes שֹׁמֵר tokens also listed under the name Shomer (v.ef.ad) and שָׁמְרָה tokens also under v.ef.ac; v.ef.ac's true count as a noun is 1 (Psa 141:3); v.eh.ac's 13 include the place Shamir (Jos 15:48) and the Levite Shamir (1Ch 24:24). Psa 77:5 שְׁמֻרוֹת: “eyelids” follows the context only. Names: entries drafted for Shemer, Shomer, Shimri, Shemariah. Left for later: Shimron son of Issachar (v.ef.an, shares its tokens with the place v.ef.am), Shimrath (v.ef.af), Shimrith (v.ef.ag; TIPNR treats her as Shomer@2Ki.12.21), Ishmerai (v.ef.aq), Shamir the Levite (v.eh.ae). Places and peoples not drafted: Samaria שֹׁמְרוֹן (v.ef.ak; 1Ki 16:24 derives it from Shemer, cited in names/shemer.json), Samaritan (v.ef.al), Shimron (v.ef.am), Shimronite (v.ef.ao), Shamir (v.eh.ad). Zero-token cross-references a.gf.ae, j.dw.af, m.di.ah, m.dw.am, v.dx.ab, v.eh.ab left out. The Peshitta renders the root by ܢܛܪ and ܡܛܪܬܐ (Mat 14:25), so there is no Syriac word of this entry.
